pairs.question: Quod sim fuscula, quod nigella, et ipsae fusco in pectore nigricent papillae, quid tum?
pairs.answer: Nox nigra, fusculae tenebrae, nocturnis colitur Venus tenebris.
pairs.derivation: The dark girl (puella fuscula) poses a rhetorical question and answers it herself. Question is the verbatim conditional setup (Quod sim fuscula... papillae) plus its interrogative cap 'quid tum?', kept contiguous so 'quid tum' has its referent. Answer starts at the operative answering clause 'Nox nigra... tenebris' (so-what: darkness is Venus's time) and stops there; the source continues with comma into elaboration ('optat nox Venerem...'), which is digression and is cut. Terminal comma normalized to a period; the heading line 'Hendecasyllabi 1.20 Loquitur puella fuscula' is scaffolding and excluded.

pairs.question: Cur ah, cur tenebrae repente nobis, cur nox exoritur, nigrescit aura?
pairs.answer: Stella est ad speculam, refulsit in te: solem lumina victa pertimescunt.
pairs.derivation: The poet asks why darkness has suddenly fallen and answers himself. Question is the verbatim interrogative line(s) 'cur ah... nigrescit aura?'. The intervening line 'An sentis, miser, an miselle, sentis?' is framing/another question and is skipped as a non-answering preamble; the answer starts at the operative answering sentence 'Stella est ad speculam, refulsit in te: solem lumina victa pertimescunt.' (the girl Stella's appearance is the cause) and stops at its full stop; following exclamations 'O claras medio die tenebras...' are cut. First-word capitalization normalized; the heading 'Hendecasyllabi 1.28 Ad Stellam puellam' and the trailing 'Neo-Latin / The Latin Library / The Classics Page' footer are scaffolding and excluded.
